item.title: Two suspects arrested after CCTV captures Nausori property theft
item.description: Two suspects have been arrested following a theft at a property in Nausori Town after CCTV footage captured two men entering the premises and stealing items. Nausori resident Feroz Khalil says the incident occurred last Wednesday at his home, located at the corner of Verrier and Gulam Nabi Streets in Nausori Town.
item.content:encoded:
Two suspects have been arrested following a theft at a property in Nausori Town after CCTV footage captured two men entering the premises and stealing items.

Nausori resident Feroz Khalil says the incident occurred last Wednesday at his home, located at the corner of Verrier and Gulam Nabi Streets in Nausori Town.

Khalil says he was working in another room when the two men entered through his open gate.

CCTV footage shows the men inside the property, with the sound of hammering heard in the background.

Khalil says one of the men took a wallet and several cartons of Powerade.

He later shared the CCTV footage publicly on Facebook in the hope that members of the public could help identify the men.

Police say the identities of the suspects are known and investigations are underway.

item.content:encoded:
A Heavy Rain Alert previously in force for the western half of Viti Levu and Mamanuca is cancelled, while the alert remains in force for the eastern half of Viti Levu including Navua-Suva-Nausori, Coral Coast, Tailevu, Naitasiri, Rakiraki, Tavua and Yasawa.

The Nadi Weather Office says a trough of low pressure associated with cloud, showers and rain lies over Fiji and is expected to affect the country until later tonight.

They say there will be occasional rain, heavy at times, and isolated thunderstorms, with rain gradually easing from later tonight.

The Weather Office says possible impacts include flash flooding in flood-prone, low-lying informal settlements and communities, as well as at businesses and Irish crossings.

They say surface flooding is also possible on streets in urban areas with poor drainage.

The Weather Office says wet roads and reduced visibility, especially during heavy downpours, could increase the risk of road accidents.

item.title: Charan Jeath Singh ordered to leave Parliament for 1.5 hours over disorderly conduct
item.description: Multi-Ethnic Minister, Charan Jeath Singh was ordered to withdraw from Parliament and its precincts for one and a half hours this morning. This is after Parliament Speaker Filimone Jitoko found Singh guilty of disorderly conduct and the use of unparliamentary expressions in relation to a Point of Order raised during Parliament's Committee of Supply debate following a heated exchange over the Tuatu
item.content:encoded:
Multi-Ethnic Minister, Charan Jeath Singh was ordered to withdraw from Parliament and its precincts for one and a half hours this morning.

This is after Parliament Speaker Filimone Jitoko found Singh guilty of disorderly conduct and the use of unparliamentary expressions in relation to a Point of Order raised during Parliament's Committee of Supply debate following a heated exchange over the Tuatua Gas Crematorium in Labasa and allegations of racial vilifications on the 16th of July.

The Speaker has also asked Singh to apologise.

The Speaker ruled that phrases such as “you listen to me” and “listen here”, were unparliamentary and disorderly.

The Speaker also found Singh’s response to Honourable Alvik Maraj’s interjection to be disorderly and in breach of the rules governing debate and the decorum of Parliament.

Meanwhile, the Speaker also found Opposition MP Alvick Maharaj guilty of disorderly conduct for shouting an interjection during Singh’s statement on different religions and practices.

Maharaj has been directed to write a letter of apology to the Office of the Speaker, conveying the same sentiments to the Chair and Members of Parliament, with the apology to be entered into the official records.

item.title: CCTV captures attempted vehicle break-in at Bayview Heights
item.description: An attempted break-in has been reported at Bayview Heights after CCTV footage captured an intruder attempting to break into a vehicle at around 3am on Thursday. The vehicle owner, Rash Jehad, says on social media that they woke up after hearing the alarm and found the intruder still attempting to gain entry.
item.content:encoded:
An attempted break-in has been reported at Bayview Heights after CCTV footage captured an intruder attempting to break into a vehicle at around 3am on Thursday.

The vehicle owner, Rash Jehad, says on social media that they woke up after hearing the alarm and found the intruder still attempting to gain entry.

According to Jehad, the intruder appeared unfazed by the alarm and only ran away after they shouted at him.

He says they contacted Nabua Police Station multiple times for assistance during the incident but claims there was no response.

The incident has raised concerns over the safety and security of residents in the area and the response to calls for police assistance during the early hours of the morning.

item.title: Nadi father raises concern over Lautoka Hospital bed shortage affecting 17-year-old son who needs CT scan
item.description: A Nadi father has raised serious concerns after his 17-year-old son, who requires further medical assessment, was unable to be transferred to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan because there was no available bed. Mohammed Kalam says his son was admitted to Nadi Hospital at around 5pm on Friday, and doctors planned to transfer him to the Lautoka hospital for a CT scan.
item.content:encoded:
A Nadi father has raised serious concerns after his 17-year-old son, who requires further medical assessment, was unable to be transferred to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan because there was no available bed.

Mohammed Kalam says his son was admitted to Nadi Hospital at around 5pm on Friday, and doctors planned to transfer him to the Lautoka hospital for a CT scan.

However, Kalam says the family was later informed that there was no spare bed available.

He says the same explanation has been given repeatedly since Friday.

Kalam says the situation is particularly concerning for his family as they live in Nadi and are waiting for his son to receive the required medical attention.

Kalam has questioned why the necessary hospital resources are not available to accommodate patients requiring specialised care.

Insert: Kalam - What is Health Minister doing Aug 16

Questions have been sent to the Minister for Health Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu regarding the delay and the availability of beds for patients requiring specialised care.

item.title: Kadavu opens first-ever taxi base to boost transport and tourism
item.description: Kadavu has opened its first-ever taxi base, with the new investment expected to improve transport services, create opportunities for local communities and support tourism and economic growth on the island. Minister f or Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Ro Filipe Tuisawau officially opened the Solo I Ra Taxi & Tours Investment Base in Namalata Village.
item.content:encoded:
Kadavu has opened its first-ever taxi base, with the new investment expected to improve transport services, create opportunities for local communities and support tourism and economic growth on the island.

Minister f or Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Ro Filipe Tuisawau officially opened the Solo I Ra Taxi & Tours Investment Base in Namalata Village.

The Solo I Ra Taxi & Tours Investment Base has been allocated 20 taxi permits, while Valelevu Brothers Investment in Daviqele Village has been allocated 15 taxi permits.

Both taxi bases have received confirmation letters for their operations.

Speaking on behalf of Namalata Village, Isireli Nuku says they are grateful to see the opening of the first taxi base in Kadavu.

Nuku also thanked the Coalition Government for supporting the initiative and helping strengthen development in villages and communities across the island.

He says the Government's support will contribute towards improving livelihoods and the wellbeing of people in Kadavu.

The new taxi operations are also expected to provide more opportunities for local businesses and improve transport options for residents and visitors.

The investment is expected to support Kadavu's tourism sector by making it easier for people to travel around the island while creating new opportunities for economic growth.
